title: His brother, baker father and travelling A.M.E. minister grandfather
summary: He describes his brother Robert, the Price Boys, his father the baker, and his grandfather who built new churches in town after town.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did you say you have brothers and sisters?

I had one brother. His name was Robert. He was two years older than I was, and we were known throughout Texas as the Price Boys. Not like the Daltons, or the Jesse James Boys; we were the Price Boys, and we were quite well known at first because/my father was a baker, you know, in Waco, and a lot of people used to come to him because he used to sell bread in our home, you see...a lot of people used to come. Then my grandfather, was a well-known A.M.E. minister, going from town to town each year, to build a new church. You see, in the south, with conditions as they were, church people...ministers, I'd say, were the liaison between the white man and the natives. Quite naturally, they had to have someone, and this minister was usually the liaison person. And...but my grandfather had fourteen kids, boys and girls, and then he had all these grandkids, naturally, and he used to go from town to town each year, when they had the quarterly Conference, which was a meeting of the various flocks; their leaders would come together, and then there was a presiding elder and a bishop, and they would determine where the assignments would be. Well, in ten years, my grandfather had an assignment in ten different cities. And he wondered why. But what my grandfather used to do was go

into a town where the conditions were deplorable and inadequate facilities for the church/ meeting; he'd take his fourteen kids and build a new church. Quite naturally that everybody wanted. So finally he asked the presiding elder why it is that he was always moved. "Well (said the elder), can't you see the handwriting on the wall? When you go into a church, and go into a new city and build a church/ everybody want you." So that was the history of doing quite a bit of traveling on his part for the first ten years of my life.
